en: The *Kalyāṇapañcaviṃśatikā-stotra*:
The glorious, primordial, self-arisen Akṣobhya Buddha, whose name is Amitaruci-amogha.

May the glorious one named Vairocana, the king of sages born of jewels, the excellent being Vajrasattva, the illustrious Prajñā who is the Vajra-realm, and those such as Noble Tārā who bring about all that is auspicious, grant you well-being whether you are moving or staying; I bow to them. (1)
The Goddess Sampatprasādā, Gaṇapatihṛdayā, Vajravidrāviṇī,
the Uṣṇīṣā Aparṇadevī, Kiṭivaravadanā, Mātṛkā of the Khecarīs, Koṭolalakṣākṣadeva, surrounded by her own hosts— the Pañcarakṣās, the divine protection.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. || 2 ||
Among the Jewels are the one named Dīpaṅkara, the Victor Maṇikusuma, the glorious Vipaśyin, Śikhin, Viśvambhu, the glorious Kakutsunda, Kanakamuni, Kāśyapa, and Śākyasiṃha;
and the present preeminent One, the possessor of all the ten powers, an ocean of supreme majesty.
May they bring about your welfare whether you are moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. || 3 ||
The glorious Āryāvalokiteśvara, the supreme among the Victors; Maitreya, the infinite treasury; the Buddha Sāmantabhadra; Mañjunātha, the great lord who wields the excellent vajra;
and the two great ones known as Sarvāghorī and Kṣitigarbha.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or standing anywhere; I bow to them. 4.
From the lotus born from the bulb of the Buddha’s empowerment, the one named Nāgadāsa—who possesses youth as his lord—emerged; from his own excellent world, he created a single light.
Having become fivefold as a single portion, he dwells eternally as the essence of the five Buddhas.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. || 5 ||

May that Wisdom, whose form is secret, born from the three-petalled lotus, may she— Nairātmyā, who takes the form of the sacred seat (pīṭha), who has accomplished manifold benefits, and who is worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Īśa— be present through the grace of the gods; she who appeared in Durgā, bestowing boons upon those who bow before her on the entire path, emerging from the unfathomable depths.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them.
From a portion of Maitrīya was born Ratnacūḍa, whose crest-jewel was the Great Forest (Vanamahat);
from him arose Jyotiratna, who, having attained auspicious light, became the vessel for the ocean of existence known as Ratnaliṅgeśvara;
then Śrīvatsa, whose greatness was established by the eight Vītarāgas, the self-manifested one (Svayambhū) of manifest form.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or standing still; I bow to them. || 7 ||
By the command of the Lord of the World, the son of the Jina named Khagañja became lotus-shaped on the bank of the Vāgmatī city to protect the wicked Gokarṇa of steadfast mind;
he is the illustrious Gokarṇeśvara here at this confluence of the Vāgmatī, who brought ruin to his own kinsmen.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or standing still; I bow to them. 8.

Frightening the enraged King of Nagas, who was like a Kulika serpent, with his stake-like [teeth] for the sake of the welfare of the worlds, the Great Lord named Kali— who is free from passion— became the form of a banner atop the Śrī mountain, moving as if in flight, bringing auspiciousness to the illustrious Sāmantas and others.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or standing anywhere; I bow to them. || 9 ||

To drink that [nectar] which has all its feet, Vajrapāṇi proceeds at the word of the Lotus-holder; for the sake of protecting the worlds, he has once again become the form of a water-jar from a portion [of that nectar].
He is the glorious one named Sarveśvara, the son of the best of Jinas, bearing a staff and a trident.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. 10.
Having made the difficult-to-understand Mañjugartavyajana— who delighted in pleasure— awakened by a beautiful woman, Mañjudeva thereafter made him a wise, great, and preeminent poet; then,
having restrained his breath and attained the state of all virtues, he became known as Gartesh.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. || 11 ||
There was a noble being named Sakalavarana-vishkambhin, adorned with ornaments and possessing the form of a fish; he was the lord of serpents who, having swiftly cast out all fear,
became known as Phani-indreshvara— one who, though free from passion, was not without fervor.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. 12.
That illustrious one, possessing a parasol [of honor], performed austerities at Oḍiyāna on its beautiful bank;
there, the Buddhist [master] named Pṛthvīgarbha suddenly established him as a resident.
Gandheśa became free from passion and stood before the Lord of the World (Lokanātha), the friend of all.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or standing still; I bow to them. 13.
Filled with joy, having attained success through his valor against the son of Amita, he blew his conch shell;
from which, by the command of the Lord of the World, Khagarbha appeared, bringing forth horses.
He, having established his own lineage, went to his city named Vikrameśa.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. || 14 ||
Where the Naga named Anusukha attained peace from Tarkshya; where the one of auspicious name, Sutirtha, and the tranquil Shantatirtha performed austerities with Parvati while dwelling in conflict;
and where the one called Shankara, the confluence of the three rivers, was practiced by Rudra whose mind longed for Durga.
May they perform auspicious deeds for you whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. 15.

Behold the confluence named Nirmala, where the king known as Tīrtha obtained the sovereignty of the earth, and the deformed hunter Kāmatīrtha reached the abode of the Lord of the Gods; and where the Vajrācārya saw the gathering brought about by the pressing of the Soma.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or standing still; I bow to them. 16.
For the poor who are devoted to worship, this is the treasure found;

for the wise, it is the sacred ford known as a mine from which knowledge is obtained; and for those of supreme intellect, it is the singular sacred ford called Knowledge, where desire is attained through ablutions just as at the sacred ford named Cintāmaṇi.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. || 17 ||
There, by those who have bathed with joy, it acquired the name "Prāmoda"; there, the Tīrtha named Sallakṣaṇa bestowed auspicious marks upon those moving within its waters;
and there, having bathed at the Tīrtha known as Abha, the Lord of the Gods named Bala conquered the island named Ākhyam.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. 18.
The goddess known as Vidyādharī, the Yoginī preceded by Vajra, Hārīta, the illustrious Hanumān, along with Gaṇapati, Mahākāla, and the one named Cūḍā— all worthy of worship;
and the goddesses beginning with Brahmāṇī, together with Hari, Sukhavarakṣa, and Nāskanda.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. 19.

Along the Vāgmatī river are the subsidiary pilgrimage sites (upatīrthas) beginning with Mūlapuccha; likewise, there are the Keśacaityas, those situated on Śaṅkhocca, and that venerable Lord Caitya gracing Jātoccayagiri.
Then there are Phullocca, Draṣṭadevī, and the locations such as Bhagavatīdhyāna and Procca.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. || 20 ||
The stūpa named Mañjuśobha, constructed by his attendants on Mount Mañjuśrī;
the natural abodes in the five divine cities fashioned by Śāntaśrī;
and the supreme stūpa at the tip of the tail where, in the city of Śāketa, he formerly proclaimed the incomparable [teaching].
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or standing still; I bow to them. || 21 ||
The one called Ādhāra resides in the heart, along with the lord of serpents and his retinue, as well as the king of obstacles and their destroyer;

and the serpent in the world of bliss— O Hari, Hari, O you whose vehicle is Hari!— in the lineage of the three worlds, may you, the sole lord of the worlds, grant me the power to behold the Lord of the World, thereby making my hopes fruitful.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. || 22 ||
Hevajra is this Saṃvara, together with his retinue and host; he is Caṇḍavīra, the Hero of the Three Worlds, and Yogāmbara.
These are the ten lords of the Krodhas, beginning with Yamāntaka who brings about the end of death.
All those who are secret and external, headed by Parmita, [are explained] in the *Nāmasaṃgīti*.
May they bring about your welfare whether you are moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. 23.
On his head, accompanied by his retinue, that Moon-like King ascended the mountain of the Setting Sun;
having cut through this lake of desolation, Mañjunātha— the abode of the world— worshipped the Supreme Victor while standing in the waters that had become tranquil, like a lotus in the finest city.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. 24.
After visiting Saṃghāvatī for the welfare of the people, he arrived at Potala; then, having been summoned by the gods, the peaceful one entered the excellent city of Lalitapura.
That glorious Vajrapāṇi was accompanied by Jaṭadhara, Hayagrīva, and the host of Gaṇeśas.
May they bring you auspiciousness whether moving or staying anywhere; I bow to them. || 25 ||
The *Kalyāṇapañcaviṃśatistuti*, extracted from the *Śrī Svayambhūpurāṇa*, is completed.
